be3ac54ea752de598fcb.text: Agreeing or disagreeing with a material viewed shows our stand on a particular

dc654bd503e90ba10bac.text: issue. It indicates whether we have the same (agreement) or a different idea (disagreement) as the one presented. There are expressions we can use to show either agreement or disagreement, such as:

rows:  I agree with you 100 percent.  I couldn't agree with you more.  That's so true.  That's for sure.  (slang) Tell me about it!  You're absolutely right.  Absolutely.  That's exactly how I feel.  Exactly.  I'm afraid I agree with James.  I have to side with Dad on this one.  No doubt about it.  (agree with the negative statement) Me neither.  (weak) I suppose so. /I guess so.  You have a point there.  I was just going to say that.

 I don't think so.  (strong) No way.  I'm afraid I disagree.  (strong) I totally disagree.  I beg to differ.  (strong) I'd say the exact opposite.  Not necessarily.  That's not always true.  That's not always the case.  No, I'm not so sure about that.

85a3d3acd7b32ade49b3.text: Moreover, there are situations when stating your reasons for agreeing or

693514a93468d77e75ec.text: disagreeing is necessary. It requires that you carefully consider arguments/evidence for and against the particular position or viewpoint raised in the material. Here are guide questions you can use.

bc3a069427a7655aa13e.text: 1. What are the strengths/advantages and weaknesses/disadvantages of _____________? 2. What evidence supports and contradicts ________________? 3. What are arguments for and counterarguments against ______________?
